group.passage: Imagine a small hospital in the hills of rural Rwanda, where a patient suddenly needs a blood transfusion. Blood products do not keep for long, and it is hard to predict how much a small hospital will need, so clinics cannot simply store large supplies. In the past, extra blood had to come by road from the capital, Kigali, often over dirt roads that became even slower to travel in the long rainy season. This could cost a patient precious hours. In 2016, Rwanda's government teamed up with Zipline, a company based in the United States, to try a different approach: drones. From a base in Muhanga District, small battery-powered planes called Zips are thrown into the air by a catapult-like launcher. Each one can fly a round trip of up to 150 kilometers while carrying as much as 1.5 kilograms of supplies. When a health worker sends an order by text message, a Zip is packed and sent on its way. It never lands. Instead, it releases a box attached to a paper parachute near the hospital and then turns back for home. Does the system work? A study published in 2022 looked at 20 health facilities. Between 2017 and 2019, drones delivered 12,733 orders of blood products to them, and 43 percent of these were emergencies. On average, a drone delivery took 49.6 minutes, about 79 minutes faster than the trip by road. The time saved ranged from 3 to 211 minutes, depending on how far away a facility was and how good its roads were. The study also found that the amount of blood that expired before it could be used dropped by 67 percent after a year. Drones are not a perfect answer, however. They depend on mobile phone networks along every route and on a steady supply of electricity. The study's authors also pointed out that no one yet knows whether the service is worth what it costs. Still, for a patient who cannot wait, an hour saved can make all the difference.

translation_zh.text:
無人機送血

想像在盧安達鄉間的山丘上有一家小醫院，有位病人突然需要輸血。血液製品無法保存很久，而且很難預測一家小醫院會需要多少，所以診所沒辦法直接大量儲存。過去，額外的血必須從首都吉佳利經公路送來，常常要走泥土路，到了漫長的雨季又更難走。這可能讓病人損失寶貴的好幾個小時。

2016 年，盧安達政府和美國公司 Zipline 合作，嘗試一種不同的方法：無人機。在穆杭加區的一個基地，名叫 Zips 的小型電池動力飛機由一種類似彈弓的發射器拋上天空。每架飛機可以來回飛行最遠 150 公里，同時載運最多 1.5 公斤的物資。醫護人員用簡訊下單後，一架 Zip 就會裝好貨物出發。它從不降落，而是在醫院附近放下一個綁著紙降落傘的箱子，然後掉頭返回基地。

這套系統有用嗎？2022 年發表的一項研究調查了 20 個醫療機構。從 2017 年到 2019 年，無人機送了 12,733 筆血液製品訂單到這些機構，其中 43% 是緊急訂單。無人機送達平均花 49.6 分鐘，比走公路快大約 79 分鐘。省下的時間從 3 分鐘到 211 分鐘不等，取決於醫療機構有多遠、道路狀況有多好。研究也發現，在使用前就過期的血液量，一年後減少了 67%。

不過，無人機並不是完美的解答。它們依賴每條航線沿途的手機網路，以及穩定的電力供應。研究作者也指出，目前還沒有人知道這項服務是否值得它的成本。儘管如此，對一位等不及的病人來說，省下一個小時就可能決定一切。
